text: A command's page states what it takes and what is worth knowing about taking it.
A read stops counting when what was read changes, unless a mechanical change carried it forward.
A removal forgets the reading of what went, for every agent, because no body stands at that path to have been read.
The index can be written again from the pages alone.
A slug reaches an id without opening the page.
A qualified name is held as its slug alone, and reads straight back into the index.
An edge kind names the index that answers it, the graph derives it here, or both, and one doing both says on each edge which it was.
A generated value is worked out when its page is created, never written by hand.
Nobody is held to reading again what a mechanical command changed, until they come to write over that file itself.
It is asked once more after time is up, so something that became true in the last gap is not read as never having.
The stamp names the paths settled since that commit.
A page the change takes away stops being reachable, and the pages the index says name it are judged though the change never names them.
This is the way back from `page-export-name`: a key written in camel and the kebab slug it is filed under name one another.
The gate is built for one phase, and which checks stand on a phase is answered where the checks are.
